Suppose \(\sqrt{2} = a/b\) in lowest terms. Then \(a^2 = 2b^2\), hence a is even, then b is even. Both even contradicts lowest terms.
If \(a^2\) is even, then a is even.

column1: Why are there infinitely many primes? (outline)
column2: Given a finite list, let N = product + 1. Each listed prime leaves remainder 1, hence divides nothing. A prime factor of N is missing from the list.

column1: Why does every integer \(n \geq 2\) have a prime factor?
column2: Its smallest divisor at least 2 is prime. A factorization of it would give a smaller divisor.
Irrational. If r + x = q, then x = q - r is rational, a contradiction.
